chunks: And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, he raised it:

A woman came to ʿUmar and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have committed fornication, so establish upon me the hadd of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' So he ordered that she be stoned. And ʿAlī, Amir al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, was present, so he said: 'Ask her how you committed fornication.'

So he asked her, and she said: 'I was in a desolate land, and severe thirst afflicted me. Then a tent appeared to me, so I went to it and found in it a Bedouin man. I asked him for water, but he refused to give me drink unless I allowed him access to myself. So I turned away from him fleeing, but the thirst became intense upon me until my eyes sank and my tongue failed. Then when the thirst overcame me, I went to him, and he gave me water and lay with me.'
Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: 'This is the one about whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: “But whoever is compelled, neither seeking nor transgressing, then there is no sin upon him.”'
She is neither one seeking it nor one transgressing, so let her go.' Then ʿUmar said: 'Were it not for ʿAlī, ʿUmar would have perished.'

key_terms.حَدَّ اللَّهِ: the prescribed legal punishment set by Allah
key_terms.غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلَا عَادٍ: without seeking the act and without transgressing its limits
key_terms.فَخَلِّ سَبِيلَهَا: release her and let her go
key_terms.فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no sin upon the compelled person

ai.seo_question: How does Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام apply the Qur’anic rule of necessity in a hadd case?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling in which Amir al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام applies the Qur’anic principle of necessity to a woman coerced by extreme thirst into sexual violation. It shows that hadd punishment is not applied where compulsion removes sin, and it highlights the Imam’s authoritative judgment in interpreting the divine ruling.
